# 1. Data
Load data files

```{r Files}
#shapefiles created in CD_data

# To make the MCP:
DB_AllGPS_sf <- sf::st_read("data_files/DB_AllGPS_sf.shp")
DB_AllGPS_sf_wgs84 <- sf::st_read("data_files/DB_AllGPS_sf_wgs84.shp")


# Lions data
#CD_sf_lions <- sf::st_read("data_files/CD_sf_lions.shp")
#CD_lions_wgs84 <- sf::st_read("data_files/CD_lions_wgs84.shp")


RandomPointsCD_data <- sf::st_read("data_files/RandomPointsCD_data_covariables.shp")
```

Now just some mild modification of the database:
```{r}
RandomPointsCD_data <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  mutate(region = ifelse(clan == "serenan" | clan == "serenas" | clan == "happyzebra", "serena", "talek")) |>
  # I need to rename those since I can use variable names with _ at the end in the models
  rename(dist_br = dst_br_, dist_wt = dst_wt_, dist_tl = dst_tl, landmark = lndmrk_)
```

Now I'll create some sub-dataset for each region created above.

Talek
```{r}
Data_talek <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  filter(region == "talek")
```

Serena
```{r}
Data_serena <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  filter(region == "serena")
```



# 2. Exploratory plots

## 2.1. IBIO 830
For IBIO830, I need to do some exploratory figures.

### a) Distribution Plot
Figure1. Distribution of the data:

```{r}
RandomPointsCD_data$case <- as.factor(RandomPointsCD_data$case)

# For the purpose of the graphs, I am adding a combined variable (region+case)
RandomPointsCD_graph <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  mutate(group = paste0(region, ".", case))
  
  
region_labels <- c("serena.0" = "A. Serena\n Available Locations",
                   "serena.1" = "B. Serena\n Used Locations",
                   "talek.0" = "C. Talek\n Available Locations",
                   "talek.1" = "D. Talek\n Used Locations")


Dist_plots <- ggplot(RandomPointsCD_graph) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = dist_br), show.legend = F) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 2, labeller = labeller(group = region_labels)) +
  labs(x = "Distance to edge of the territory (m)",
       y = "Counts") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15))

Dist_plots
```


### b) Boxplots
The prediction is that hyenas are selecting den locations closer to human communities. Here, human communities will be illustrated as th edge of the territory

For IBIO830: I will use this boxplot, as it looks like it is significant. 
```{r}
loc_labels <- c("0" = "Available Locations", "1" = "Used Locations")

# ggplot:
Boxplot_talek <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  filter(region == "talek") |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(aes(y = dist_br, x = case, fill = case), show.legend = F) +
  geom_jitter(aes(y = dist_br, x = case), show.legend = F, alpha = 0.03) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = loc_labels) +
  labs(y = "Distance to edge of the territory (m)",
       x = "") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15))  
Boxplot_talek
```


```{r}
# ggplot:
Boxplot_serena <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  filter(region == "serena") |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(aes(y = dist_br, x = case, fill = case), show.legend = F) +
  geom_jitter(aes(y = dist_br, x = case), show.legend = F, alpha = 0.03) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = loc_labels) +
  labs(y = "Distance to edge of the territory (m)",
       x = "") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 15))  
  
Boxplot_serena
```

Saving them:
```{r}
ggsave('IBIO830/Dist_plots.tiff', plot = Dist_plots, height = 10, width = 10)
ggsave('IBIO830/Boxplot_talek.tiff', plot = Boxplot_talek, height = 5, width = 5)
ggsave('IBIO830/Boxplot_serena.tiff', plot = Boxplot_serena, height = 5, width = 5)
```

# 3. Modelling the RSF

ALSO, we need to control for the obs effort (some years field team would go more on obs vs other years/season). I guess with year as a random, and month as a covariable, it does control for this...

------------------------------------------------------------------------
Quick tips for RSF modelling

-   Treat landcover as a categorical predictor (factor) in your logistic/conditional logistic RSF (used vs available).

-   If you used a very fine raster (10 m) but your hyena den location accuracy is coarse (GPS error), consider buffering points or using a majority focal window to reduce misclassification from single-pixel noise.

-   If you want multi-year matching (landcover year of den use), pick the dataset year accordingly (Copernicus 2019 / WorldCover 2020 / MODIS yearly).

## 3.1. RSF model


### brms
Will first do the distance to border for Talek dens
```{r}
Data_talek$year <- as.double(Data_talek$year)
```


```{r talek model}
Talek_RSF1 <- brm(case ~ scale(dist_br) + (1|year),
                  data = Data_talek, 
                  family = bernoulli(),
                  cores = 4, 
                  chains = 4)

summary(Talek_RSF1)
conditional_effects(Talek_RSF1)
```


### lme4

```{r}
talek_rsf <- glm(case ~ scale(dist_br), 
                 family = binomial, 
                 data = Data_talek)

summary(talek_rsf)
tab_model(talek_rsf)
```

```{r}
ggpredict(talek_rsf, terms = "dist_br") |> 
  plot()
```


```{r rsf with lme4}
talek_rsf2 <- glmer(case ~ scale(dist_br) + (1|year), 
                      family = "binomial", 
                      data = Data_talek)
summary(talek_rsf2)
tab_model(talek_rsf2)
```

```{r}
ggpredict(talek_rsf2, terms = "dist_br") |> 
  plot()
```














## 3.2. Distance to Talek model

```{r}
CD_RSF_data_tl <- RandomPointsCD_data |>
  filter(clan == "talek")


brm_RSF_tl <- brm(case ~ dst_tl + year + (1|year),
                  data = CD_RSF_data_tl, 
                  family = bernoulli(),
                  cores = 4, 
                  chains = 4)

brm_RSF_tl <- readRDS("brms_models/brm_RSF_tl.rds")

```

```{r}

summary(brm_RSF_tl)
plot(conditional_effects(brm_RSF_tl), points = T)
```
